results.name: mult5_vs_other_multiple_gap
results.description: In sets whose examples share both a multiple-of-5/10 property and some other multiple-of-m property (m in 3..12, e.g. 90,45 share x5 and x9), yes-rate for targets that are multiples of the shared 5/10 (but not of the other shared m) minus targets that are multiples of another shared m but not of the shared 5/10; observed > null means the model's single 'multiples' salience under-differentiates base-10 multiples from other multiples (people strongly prefer x5/x10 rules).
results.code:
# name: mult5_vs_other_multiple_gap
# description: In sets whose examples share both a multiple-of-5/10 property and some other multiple-of-m property (m in 3..12, e.g. 90,45 share x5 and x9), yes-rate for targets that are multiples of the shared 5/10 (but not of the other shared m) minus targets that are multiples of another shared m but not of the shared 5/10; observed > null means the model's single 'multiples' salience under-differentiates base-10 multiples from other multiples (people strongly prefer x5/x10 rules).
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = np.zeros(len(t), bool); b = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
    for s in pd.unique(sets):
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        if len(xs) < 2:
            continue
        sh = [m for m in range(3, 13) if all(x % m == 0 for x in xs)]
        five = [m for m in sh if m in (5, 10)]
        oth = [m for m in sh if m not in (5, 10)]
        if not five or not oth:
            continue
        idx = sets == s
        h5 = np.zeros(len(t), bool); ho = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
        for m in five:
            h5 |= (t % m == 0)
        for m in oth:
            ho |= (t % m == 0)
        a |= idx & h5 & ~ho
        b |= idx & ho & ~h5
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: parity_violation_odd_vs_even_set_asymmetry
results.description: Yes-rate for even targets when all examples are odd minus yes-rate for odd targets when all examples are even (multi-example sets only); observed > null means people tolerate parity violations of odd sets more than of even sets beyond what the model's single shared parity salience predicts, observed < null the reverse.

results.name: between_set_mean_spread
results.description: Standard deviation across sets (those asked with >=4 distinct targets) of the set-level mean yes-rate; observed > null means the model compresses set-to-set differences in overall willingness to say yes (e.g. near-zero for 84,94,34 vs high for 90,100,5), observed < null means it exaggerates them.

results.name: shared_final_digit_violation_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets NOT ending in the final digit that all (>=2) examples share (e.g. 84,94,34 -> 40..49); observed < null means the model over-produces yes for final-digit violators (it lets parity/contained-digit/span overlap compensate where people treat the shared final digit as a hard rule), observed > null the reverse.

results.name: within_set_target_spread
results.description: Mean, over sets asked with >=8 distinct targets, of the standard deviation of per-target yes-rates within the set; observed > null means people discriminate among targets of the same set more sharply (more all-or-none) than the model's graded overlap predicts, observed < null means the model over-discriminates.

results.name: majority_final_digit_effect
results.description: In sets where a final digit is shared by a strict majority (>=2, >half) but not all examples (e.g. 69,9,39,21 -> '9'), yes-rate for targets ending in that digit minus other targets in those sets; observed > null means the model (which only counts properties shared by ALL examples) under-produces partial/majority-feature similarity generalization.
results.code:
# name: majority_final_digit_effect
# description: In sets where a final digit is shared by a strict majority (>=2, >half) but not all examples (e.g. 69,9,39,21 -> '9'), yes-rate for targets ending in that digit minus other targets in those sets; observed > null means the model (which only counts properties shared by ALL examples) under-produces partial/majority-feature similarity generalization.
def test_statistic(df):
    sets = df["number_set"].astype(str).values
    t = df["target"].astype(int).values
    r = df["rating"].values.astype(float)
    a = np.zeros(len(t), bool); b = np.zeros(len(t), bool)
    for s in pd.unique(sets):
        xs = [int(x) for x in s.split(",")]
        n = len(xs)
        if n < 3:
            continue
        fds = [x % 10 for x in xs]
        maj = [d for d in set(fds) if fds.count(d) >= 2 and fds.count(d) * 2 > n and fds.count(d) < n]
        if not maj:
            continue
        idx = sets == s
        has = np.isin(t % 10, maj)
        a |= idx & has
        b |= idx & ~has
    if a.sum() == 0 or b.sum() == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float(r[a].mean() - r[b].mean())

results.name: contained_digit_only_effect
results.description: In sets whose examples all contain a digit d but share no final digit (e.g. 20,32,92 share '2'), among targets of the examples' shared parity (if any), yes-rate for targets containing d minus those not containing d; observed < null means the model over-weights the shared contained-digit feature (people largely ignore it), observed > null means it under-weights it.

results.name: full_match_out_of_span_rate
results.description: Yes-rate for targets lying outside the examples' [min,max] span that nonetheless have every parity/prime/square/cube/power/multiple/final-digit/contained-digit property shared by all examples (requires >=1 such shared property); observed > null means the model's span feature penalizes rule-consistent out-of-span targets too much, observed < null too little.
